title: Best Invitation Designers (2026): How to Hire One
description: How to hire an invitation designer for weddings, parties or events: print and digital invitations, how to brief it, price factors and red flags.
intro: Invitations set the tone for weddings, birthdays, corporate events and parties. A designer can create a matching set, from save-the-dates to invitations and signs, in print or digital formats. Orders go wrong when details change after printing, the file does not match the printer's size, or digital versions are forgotten. This guide helps you order invitations that look right and arrive on time.

faq.q: Should invitations be printed or digital?
faq.a: Both work. Printed invitations feel special; digital ones are faster and cheaper to send. Many people order a printed set and a digital version from the same design.
Who is hosting, what the event is, date and time, place, dress code if any, and how to reply. Keep extra details for a separate card or website.
Yes. Save-the-dates, menus, place cards, programs and signs can share the same design. Ordering them together keeps them consistent.
Early enough to allow design, revisions, printing and mailing. Printed invitations usually need several weeks before the event.

faq.q: Will I get an editable file?
faq.a: Ask for one if details might change, or if you want to reuse the design.
